title: Conserved energetic changes drive function in an ancient protein fold.
authors: Wells, Malcolm L; Lu, Chenlin; Sultanov, Daniel; Weber, Kyle C; Gong, Zhen; Glasgow, Anum
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过MD模拟等方法研究细菌转录因子与其结构同源蛋白的保守能量蓝图差异，聚焦TF-DNA调控功能相关的变构网络，虽非直接建模TF-DNA结合，但方法可迁移至本课题。
abstract: Many protein sequences occupy similar three-dimensional structures known as protein folds. In nature, protein folds are well-conserved over the course of evolution, such that there are 100,000 times as many extant protein sequences than there are folds. Despite their common shapes, similar protein folds can adopt wide-ranging functions, raising the question: are protein folds so strongly conserved for the purpose of maintaining function-driving energetic changes in protein families? Here we show that a set of key energetic relationships in a family of bacterial transcription factors (TFs) is conserved using high-resolution hydrogen exchange/mass spectrometry, bioinformatics, X-ray crystallography, and molecular dynamics simulations. We compared the TFs to their anciently diverged structural homologs, the periplasmic binding proteins (PBPs), expecting that protein families that share the same fold and bind the same sugars would have similar energetic responses. Surprisingly, our findings reveal the opposite: the "energetic blueprints" of the PBPs and the TFs are largely distinct, with the allosteric network of the TFs evolving specifically to support the functional requirements of genome regulation, versus conserved interactions with membrane transport machinery in PBPs. These results demonstrate how the same fold can be adapted for different sense/response functions via family-specific energetic requirements - even when responding to the same chemical trigger. Understanding the evolutionarily conserved energetic blueprint for a protein family provides a roadmap for designing functional proteins de novo, and will help us treat aberrant protein behavior in conserved domains in disease-related drug targets, where engineering selectivity is challenging.
abstract_zh: 许多蛋白质序列占据相似的三维结构，称为蛋白质折叠 (protein folds)。在自然界中，蛋白质折叠在进化过程中高度保守，以至于现存蛋白质序列的数量比折叠类型多出10万倍。尽管形状相似，相似的蛋白质折叠可以承担广泛的功能，这引发了一个问题：蛋白质折叠是否如此强烈地保守，以维持蛋白质家族中驱动功能的能量变化？在此，我们展示了通过高分辨率氢交换/质谱、生物信息学、X射线晶体学和分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，一组细菌转录因子 (transcription factors, TFs) 家族中的关键能量关系得以保守。我们将这些TFs与其古老分化的结构同源物——周质结合蛋白 (periplasmic binding proteins, PBPs) 进行比较，预期共享相同折叠并结合相同糖类的蛋白质家族会具有相似的能量响应。令人惊讶的是，我们的发现揭示了相反的情况：PBPs和TFs的“能量蓝图”在很大程度上是截然不同的，TFs的变构网络特异性地进化以支持基因组调控的功能需求，而PBPs则保守地与膜转运机制相互作用。这些结果证明了同一折叠如何通过家族特异性的能量需求适应不同的感知/响应功能——即使响应相同的化学触发物。理解蛋白质家族进化上保守的能量蓝图为从头设计功能性蛋白质提供了路线图，并将帮助我们在疾病相关药物靶点的保守结构域中治疗异常蛋白质行为，在这些靶点中，工程选择性具有挑战性。
